notes: Non-discriminating: secret refusal, lesson reinforcement in end-of-day, journal/decision/next checks pass without the skill too. The sample repo's CLAUDE.md rules and self-describing lesson metadata already teach a capable agent most of the format.

Where the skill made the difference: the empty-file check at start of day (baseline missed the emptied backlog entirely), problems surfaced before the task list, a step-by-step close report including the unlanded-work safety check, timed journal headings, and flagging a recurring lesson for promotion.

Correct judgment beyond the checks: with the skill, close-task did not bump the lesson count because the lesson came from the same task. The original assertion expecting seen 2 was wrong and was replaced.
Behavior difference not graded: the baseline start-day edited tasks/active.md (removed the stored PR status) during what should be a read-only briefing; the skill run flagged it without editing.
Cost: with the skill, about 6-8k more tokens and 10-15s more per run (reads SKILL.md plus one routine and runs the script).
Gaps: none of the cases use a real git repo, so check-commit, the hooks and backend cleanup aren't exercised. Only 1 run per configuration, so there's no variance data.
